skill.name: writing-video-prompts
skill.description: Writes model-specific motion prompts for video clips using briefs, frames, source videos, or storyboards. It covers camera direction, timing, physical action, references, dialogue, and audio without generating video.
skill.summary: Turns settled video concepts and media into precise, model-specific clip prompts.
skill.author: supercmohq

content.value_statement: Video models need different motion, camera, timing, reference, and audio instructions. This skill converts settled clip concepts into focused prompts for supported model families.
actual_capabilities: Writes one model-specific text prompt for each requested video clip.
Adapts prompt structure for Seedance, Veo, Gemini Omni, Kling, Grok, and Wan families.
Converts storyboard panels into timed cuts with camera, action, and continuity direction.
Labels start frames, end frames, people, products, and references using model-specific conventions.
Coordinates dialogue, ambience, effects, and native audio markers with visual beats.
Flags timing, hand-count, media-input, and physical-continuity conflicts before rendering.
limitations: It writes prompts only and does not generate, render, or edit video files.
It needs a settled clip concept, duration, and media roles for the most precise result.
Unsupported models receive guidance based on the closest documented model family.
Prompt quality cannot overcome weak source media or inherent model rendering limits.

use_cases.title: Direct a Product Clip
use_cases.description: Turn product actions, camera framing, dialogue, and references into a focused prompt that preserves packaging and physical continuity.

use_cases.title: Convert Storyboards into Cuts
use_cases.description: Read each storyboard panel as a timed cut and produce model-specific motion, camera, performance, and audio direction.

use_cases.title: Repair an Unstable Prompt
use_cases.description: Simplify overloaded motion, correct timing, prevent duplicate limbs, and align references with the selected video model.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Single-Shot Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a video prompt for [model]. The clip lasts [duration]. Show [subject] performing [single action] in [setting]. Use [framing] with [camera movement].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one continuous clip without reference media.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Start Frame
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a [duration] prompt for [model] using the supplied image as the opening frame. Preserve [fixed details]. Animate [motion] with [camera behavior] and [audio].
prompt_templates.scenario: A creator has a fixed composition and needs precise motion direction.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Storyboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this storyboard for a [duration] [model] clip. Create one timed cut per panel. Preserve visible positions, assign one action per cut, and include camera and audio direction.
prompt_templates.scenario: A multi-panel storyboard must become a structured sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose and Rewrite a Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [model] prompt against the supplied media and duration. Identify timing, continuity, reference, camera, motion, and audio conflicts. Then rewrite one prompt per clip.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced revision of prompts that produce unstable or inconsistent video.

output_examples.input: Write a five-second Veo prompt for a ceramic cup on a table. Use a slow push-in and room sound.
output_examples.output: Close-up with a slow push-in. A matte ceramic cup rests on a wooden table as steam curls steadily upward in warm morning light. Ambient noise: quiet room tone and a soft ceramic tap.

output_examples.input: Turn a two-panel skincare storyboard into an eight-second Kling prompt with one spoken line.
output: Cut 1 (0-4s): Medium close-up. The creator lifts the closed serum bottle beside her face while the camera tracks gently forward.
She says, "This is my morning essential." Soft room tone and a quiet fabric movement.
Cut 2 (4-8s): Macro close-up. Her free hand tilts the intact bottle toward the light while the camera holds steady. The label remains clear.

output_examples.input: Fix a prompt where a person holds a phone, opens a jar, and applies cream in one arm-length shot.
output_examples.output: The requested framing leaves only one hand free, so the full action cannot remain physically consistent. Reframe as locked off or split the opening and application into separate clips.

best_practices: Provide the target model, clip duration, intended action, and the role of each media asset.
Use one clear physical action and one camera move per beat.
Verify timed beats add up exactly and preserve visible positions between cuts.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated actions, several camera moves, and dense dialogue in one short beat.
Do not restate every visible detail when a start frame or storyboard already fixes the composition.
Do not ask this skill to render a finished video or guarantee model output quality.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos?
faq.answer: No. It produces text prompts and media-order guidance for use with a separate video generation service.

faq.question: Which video models are supported?
faq.answer: It includes guides for Seedance 2.0, Veo 3.1, Gemini Omni, Kling 3.0 Pro, Grok Imagine Video, and Wan 2.7 families.

faq.question: Can it work from a storyboard?
faq.answer: Yes. It can analyze panels, preserve rendered positions, and write one timed cut per panel.

faq.question: Can it use start frames and reference images?
faq.answer: Yes. It labels and orders supported media according to the selected model guide.

faq.question: Does it handle dialogue and sound?
faq.answer: Yes. It places exact dialogue, ambience, effects, and audio markers according to each model's prompt format.

faq.question: What happens when the brief has too many actions?
faq.answer: It identifies the duration conflict and returns the beats that fit instead of compressing unstable actions.
